info.title: AuctionIt API
info.description:
REST API behind the AuctionIt admin console, bidder portal and client portal.

## Authentication
1. `POST /auth/login` with login name + password. When 2FA is on, an OTP is sent and the response asks for it.
2. `POST /auth/login/verify-otp` returns `{ user, sessionToken }` and also sets the session cookie.
3. Send the token on every call as `Authorization: Bearer <sessionToken>` (use **Authorize** above),
   or rely on the `session_<appId>` cookie, where `appId` comes from the `X-App-Id` header
   (or `?app_id=` for top-level navigations).

Sessions are opaque random tokens, not JWTs.

## Access control
Each operation lists its access rule, derived from the route's real middleware:
- **Login required** — any authenticated user.
- **Permissions** — permission keys from `@auctionit/authz` (see `docs/permissions.md`). Admin roles use the matrix like any other role.
  The same rule is machine-readable in the `x-permissions` extension.
- **Portal role** — bidder-portal or client-portal users only (`x-portal-role`).

## Errors
| Status | Body | When |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | `ValidationErrorBody` `{ error, fieldErrors }` | Query/body failed validation |
| 401 | `AuthErrorBody` with `code: "session_invalid"` | Missing or expired session — clients should log out |
| 403 | `AuthErrorBody` with `code: "permission_denied"` | Logged in but not allowed |
| 404 | `ErrorBody` `{ error }` | Entity not found |
| 500 | `ErrorBody` | Unexpected server error |

## Realtime
Live bidding also uses Socket.IO and a Server-Sent Events fallback (`/live/stream`). Socket.IO events
are not expressible in OpenAPI; see `docs/api/README.md`.

Operations marked **⚠️ Not yet documented** are real routes that only have auto-derived metadata so far.

post.description:
Checks the username and password of an active user. Legacy MD5 password hashes are upgraded to bcrypt on success.

**2FA on (default, `AUTH_2FA_ENABLED`)**: a 6-digit OTP is generated and sent — by **SMS** for bidder/client portal roles, by **email** for staff roles — and the response is `requiresOtp: true` with a `challengeId`. The OTP is valid for 15 minutes and allows 5 attempts. Continue with `POST /auth/login/verify-otp`.

**2FA off**: the session is created immediately; the response carries `user` + `sessionToken` and sets the `session_<appId>` cookie (see below).

**Session**: one session per user — a new login replaces the previous session token. The token lives 7 days and is set as an httpOnly, `SameSite=Lax` cookie named `session_<appId>` (`appId` from the `X-App-Id` header, sanitised; plain `session` when absent), `Secure` in production. Any later request may authenticate with that cookie or with `Authorization: Bearer <sessionToken>`.

**Throttling**: failed passwords are counted per login name (10 per 15 min) and per client IP (50 per 15 min); beyond that the endpoint answers 429 with a `Retry-After` header until the oldest failure ages out. A successful login clears the login-name counter.

**Access:** public — no login required.

patch.description:
Partial update of auction settings. Allowed at any auction status (draft, published — including live — or closed). Writes apply immediately — a published auction stays published and does not need re-publishing. Sealed-bid settings (date/start/end) can be changed at any time the auction is draft or published — even while the window is open or after it has closed, moving it forward to a later time or a future day. If any sealed bids exist on the auction when the window actually changes, they are disabled (soft-deleted) as part of the same update, so bidders rebid under the new schedule. The sealed-bid date can't be before today or after the auction date — its time of day is otherwise independent of the auction's/lots' schedule. `auctionDate` can only change when no lot on the auction has any bids — remove all bids from every lot first (via the lot-correction `remove_all_bids` type), then retry. Changing the date of a closed (necessarily bid-free) auction republishes it on the new date (`status` back to `published`, `closedAt` cleared, and any stale no-bid-extension state on its lots reset). The consolidated EMD amount can only change while the auction is published or closed (not draft/archived), and only while no bidder is attached to any lot on the auction (detach everyone first) — unlike a per-range amount, it has no narrower scope to check. `clientId` cannot be changed. Changing no-bid extension settings is synced onto the lots.

**Access:** login required.
- Requires any of: `module.auctions`, `auctions.read`.

get.description:
Server→client fallback for the Socket.IO channel; bids still go through the REST endpoints. EventSource can't set headers, so pass `?app_id=` and the matching session cookie authenticates. Up to 25 auctions per stream; each is joined in the same audience room its socket would get (admin / client / public bidder), and auctions the user may not watch are reported with `live:error` instead of failing the stream.

The stream starts with `retry: <sseRetryMs>`, then:
- `live:meta` — `{ transport: "sse", serverTime, auctionIds }` (the auctions actually joined).
- `live:error` — `{ error: "not_authorized", auctionId }` for each denied auction.
- `live:snapshot` — `LiveAuctionSnapshot`: once per auction on join (personal projection for bidders), then shared room snapshots after extensions and on periodic resync.
- `live:lot` — `LiveLotDelta` after every accepted bid / proxy (projected for the room).
- `live:standing` — `LiveStanding`, bidders only: private `{ auctionId, lotId, yourStatus, currentBid, seq, rev, yourRank?, yourBid? }` when their standing may have changed.
- `live:ping` — `{ serverTime }` (epoch ms) heartbeat; use it to detect a silent stream.
- `live:close` — `{ reason }` just before the server ends the stream (e.g. `transport_mode_changed`).

**Access:** login required.
